minutes.headline: Commission voted to send $300-a-day violation notices to 390 Howard Street over uncontrolled erosion; Sunset Lane tree hearing continued.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission met by Zoom and handled hearings, administrative determinations, certificates of compliance and enforcement. The longest discussions were tree removal and erosion at 160 Sunset Lane (continued to Sept 18) and worsening erosion at 390 Howard Street, where a daily violation fine was moved. Late items approved use of the town purchase order for a bridge repair and a request to the planning board for GIS hours, and the agent reported on the paperwork backlog and a new part-time hire.

budget_items.what_was_said: Motion for a per-day fine until erosion controls are restored; a member noted the bylaw caps the fine and a new notice must be written and mailed each day.
A member compared the cost of small whip plantings against nursery container trees.
figures_as_heard: a couple hundred dollars a tree

budget_items.what_was_said: Commission allowed a volunteer to use the existing purchase order for materials, with prior notice of an approximate amount.
The commission authorized a request to the planning board to release GIS hours for updating trail maps.
The new hire's hours were reduced due to budget, with part of the time going to minute-taking, and the previous minute-taker position no longer budgeted.
A grant awarded in 2023 is progressing, with purchase orders being generated to start consultant work; another grant is being closed out.

decisions.decision: Applicant at 160 Sunset Lane is expected to return on Sept 18 with a native planting plan to quickly revegetate the eroding slope; proposed conditions included removing the three trees nearest the dock with roots left in place and replacing removed trees three to one with whips.
Agent to send a certified violation notice with a deadline to 390 Howard Street, and to ask DEP and other agencies about escalating the project.
Commission members agreed the agent may reach out to DEP for advice, and that the ANRAD could be denied for lack of information if the applicant keeps continuing it.
Violation letter for 40 Fire Road 12 to be moved to the top of the agent's priority list, with 390 Howard Street a close second.
New part-time office assistant starts the next day after select board approval.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted to issue a per-day violation notice at 390 Howard Street until erosion controls are restored and approved by the office.
The 160 Sunset Lane tree removal determination was continued to September 18, pending a more detailed erosion control and replanting plan.
The 390 Howard Street abbreviated notice of resource area delineation hearing was continued to October 2.
Three certificates of compliance were approved, along with a negative determination for a driveway and sewer connection and a notice of project change at 10 Sunset Ave.
The Commission allowed use of the town purchase order for bridge repairs at Larkin Town Forest and asked the planning board to release 2024 GIS hours for trail maps.

why_it_matters: Erosion at 390 Howard Street is the kind of unresolved site problem that can drain into nearby waterways, and the Commission is now using fines and agency escalation, not further hearings, to force a fix.

The Commission's enforcement relies on a bylaw cap and a notice written and mailed each day, and the agent's workload and a part-time hire with reduced hours affect how quickly violation letters and decisions get out.
watch_next: September 18: the 160 Sunset Lane hearing resumes with a native planting and erosion control plan.
October 2: the continued 390 Howard Street delineation hearing, where the Commission said the application could be denied for lack of information if it keeps being continued.
